I am 38 years old, finished middle school, and farm about 12 mu of land here in Quzhou County. My family has always farmed this plot, and over the years I have figured out what works. I do not have money to waste on experiments, but I also cannot afford to fall behind my neighbors.

It is mid-April now. The winter wheat I sowed last October is already knee-high and green. I am not worried about it — I used improved seed from the supply shop, rotary-tilled the ground before sowing, and put down about 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as basal dressing. I will irrigate three more times before harvest in early June: once now at jointing, once at heading, and once at grain filling. I also sprayed herbicide once in early spring and will do two more pesticide passes if I see aphids or rust. I expect about 500 kg per mu if the weather holds. I learned from the extension guy that 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is enough, but honestly I put down closer to 18 kg because last year when I cut back the yield dropped and I regretted it. Better to waste a little fertilizer than to lose a whole crop.

For summer maize, I will plant right after wheat harvest — probably within two or three days. The window is tight, so I will not till the soil; I will sow directly into the wheat stubble. Everyone around here does no-tillage for maize now. I will buy hybrid seed, probably Denghai or something similar from the shop. I will apply compound fertilizer at sowing and that is usually enough for the whole season — maybe 80 jin per mu. The extension people say you can topdress urea at the big-flare stage, but I usually do not bother unless the plants look yellow. I will irrigate two or three times depending on the rain. Three pesticide applications: one herbicide, two insecticide. I expect around 550 kg per mu.

I also keep 2 mu of cotton. Cotton prices have been decent lately, and it spreads my risk. I rotary-till those 2 mu in late April and plant improved cotton seed. Cotton needs a lot of spraying — I do about 14 applications through the season for bollworms, aphids, and weeds. I irrigate three times. Yield is lower than grain, about 275 kg per mu of seed cotton, but the cash is good and the cotton stalks make good fuel.

I thought about planting more cotton, but my wife and I cannot handle more than 2 mu of it — the spraying alone takes too much time. The wheat-maize double crop basically runs itself with the machinery we can hire. So 10 mu wheat-maize and 2 mu cotton it is.
